events.full_description:
WPFW listeners: Bring the family to the 9th Annual WPFW 5K Run/Walk for Total Fitness! Rain or Shine - join warm-ups, a scenic 5K walk/run, and fitness/wellness classes for physical, mental, and emotional health. Children under 12 can do a 1K, play games (kickball, jump rope, 4 Corners, etc.) and receive participation certificates.

Join a Tai Chi, Yoga, Functional Strength Training, Line Dance, Double Dutch and Meditation class. Have fun playing games for adults such as Tug Of War, Dodge Ball and more.  Or, you may prefer playing a game of Chess, Checkers or Backgammon. There is something for everybody, young and older. 

Enjoy nourishing snacks, water, and a soundtrack of great music as you walk, run, stretch, and connect with community. 100% of proceeds benefit WPFW’s programming — your registration directly supports the voices, artists, and justice-focused coverage you love. 

Sign up, bring friends, and help keep Jazz and Justice on the air.

Registration fee: $35 — 100% of proceeds support WPFW, your home for Jazz and Justice

CLICK HERE TO REGISTER

Questions: 202-888-5484 or info@wpfw.org

events.title: DC Statehood Townhall Lecture on Josephine Butler, co-founder of DC Statehood Party
events.short_description: General Election to General Strike: the history of the fight for self-determination. DC Statehood could tip the balance of power in the US which is why it is not tenable w/o a demand. Join DC's foremost historian Dr. C.R. Gibbs @ Busboys and Poets 450 K st 9/12/26 from 1pm - 3pm RSVP @ DC Statehood Townhall on Eventbrite
events.full_description: Josephine Butler was an active volunteer with the local Democratic Party. However, she was disenchanted with the police violence at the 1968 DNC in Chicago and decided "there was something better I could be doing with my time politically". That was the DC Statehood Party which Butler co-founded in 1971 with Julius Hobson. They not only challenged the community's lack of congressional representation but successfully fought a major highway and an interstate that would have ran through Northeast DC. These plans would have displaced thousands of families in the area.  Butler was co-chair of Friends of Meridian Hill, a group dedicated to rehabilitating Malcolm X Park. This was rooted in efforts to create safe, beautiful spaces for community gathering and family and children enjoyment. In 1994, she introduced President Clinton at an Earth Day speech in the park. Clinton later awarded Butler the National Partnership-Leadership Award. The following year, she organized an Earth Day parade of 4,000 people to the US Capitol where she addressed a crowd of 250,000.  Josephine Butler died in 1997, but the lessons from her legacy of self-determination still echoes in the face of a rogue, authoritarian regime today.

events.title: WPFW 4th 50th Year Benefit Concert: An Afternoon of Jazz & Justice
events.short_description: Join us for another afternoon of great jazz featuring the sounds of bassists Herman Burney and Kriss Funn.
events.full_description:
​With a tip of the hat to the late, great bassist Ray Brown, WPFW is proud to present Two Bass Hit, our fourth 50th year benefit concert. Join us for an afternoon of smooth vibes featuring two of the DMV’s finest bassists.

Two Bass Hit features Washington’s own Herman Burney jamming alongside trombonist Reginald Cyntje, while Baltimore’s Kris Funn brings back his DC JazzPrix-winning group, the CornerStore.

WPFW is building a better world, one live jazz concert at a time. Don’t miss it!

events.title: Jazz and Justice Festival
events.short_description: Seven hours of live music on the hill, and we put the whole thing on the air.
events.full_description:
Seven hours of live music on the hill, and we put the whole thing on the air. Edwin Ortiz & La Mafia Del Guaguanco open the dance floor, Blue Note trumpeter Brandon Woody follows, then Grammy-nominated MuMu Fresh, Proverbs Reggae Band, and Be'la Dona closing it out with go-go. Between the sets, the programmers you hear all week step out from behind the glass. Across 15th Street at the Josephine Butler Parks Center, documentary screenings and community discussions run from one until seven, alongside an elders circle, yoga, and art.

The Sunday drum circle opens the day at 12:30, as it has on this hill since 1965. It's also the park's 90th anniversary weekend.

 No ticket, no RSVP. Bring a blanket and bring your people.

Full lineup, set times, and how to get there: https://www.wpfwdc.org/jazz-and-justice-festival
